Hi Logan,

Great meeting yesterday — Acera is excited to bundle our connector with Redwood Dedicated for a joint reseller path. Before we lock the pilot MOU, two quick questions on how Redwood typically handles multi-partner crediting when a customer buys a bundled SKU that includes both an ISV license and Redwood hosting:

- Revenue split: does Redwood prefer a fixed percentage split on net invoice or a margin-based carve? We want something simple for year one but scalable.
- Intro/lead credit sequencing: if an integrator (consultancy) introduces the customer but Acera closes the integration and demo, who gets the referral credit? We often see both partners expecting full credit.

I attached a draft term sheet and a short demo outline. Can you point us to your preferred registration/first-touch process (HubSpot link) and any standard clawback window you operate under?

Proposed timing: quick sync Tues or Wed this week and then we can iterate the term sheet.

Thanks,

Eleanor — thanks for the clear summary and the term sheet. Short answers and suggested next steps: 

- Revenue split: for simplicity on pilots we prefer a fixed percentage on net invoice and reconcile at renewal. Typical starting point is 60/40 (partner:Redwood) for reseller-led transactions, adjustable by volume tiers.
- Intro sequencing: we rely on partner registration + first-touch timestamp in HubSpot. Whoever registers the opportunity first gets primary referral credit. If an integrator signs up and later the ISV provides critical technical work, we support co-sell credits via a secondary split.

I'll propose the following for the pilot: 60/40 base split to the registering partner, 30-day co-sell window where both partners can claim technical/demo credit (resulting in a 50/50 split if both materially contributed), and a 90-day clawback for chargebacks/returns.

Marissa / Ben — looped you in for any ops/legal caveats before I send this back to Acera. Eleanor — can you confirm HubSpot is the right place to register (we'll send the link and a short upload checklist)?

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference

Logan / Eleanor — quick policy note from Partner Ops and a redline suggestion on the attached term sheet. High level recommendations: 

- Attribution: primary credit = first valid registration in HubSpot (we consider registration valid when we have customer name, domain, estimated ACV, and partner contact).
- Co-sell window: 30 calendar days from registration for dual-credit claims. After 30 days, primary credit stands unless both partners sign a co-sell confirmation form.
- Commission structure: base 60/40 to the registered partner, but add performance tiers at 6 and 12 months (e.g., +5% at $250k ARR net-new).
- Clawback: standard 120 days on billed revenue, but given the bundled nature we can contractually shorten to 90 days for pilots (recommended). We should document how to prorate split if partial refunds occur.
- Edge case: reseller + ISV + consultancy (three-party deal) — propose we require an explicit multi-party split agreement signed at registration to avoid retro disputes.

Attached: term_sheet_redline_Acera.pdf (redlines). I'll drop a HubSpot registration checklist link in a follow-up.

-Marissa
Head of Partner Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Adding a couple technical/ops clarifications that often come up during renewals or invoicing: 

- Demo-credit: we give a one-off demo credit (up to $5k value) to the partner that executes the technical demo that leads to signed SOW. If both partners run demos, ops will ask for timestamps and customer attestations; in those cases split to 50/50 unless otherwise pre-agreed.
- Billing flow for bundled SKUs: Redwood invoices for hosting; ISV invoices separately for licenses. Net invoice split is easiest for accounting but requires clear E2E pricing on the partner term sheet to avoid double-counting discounts.
- Legal ask: require Acera to accept our partner MSA addendum concerning data security and triage response SLAs. We can bundle that as an appendix.

Happy to jump on a quick 20m call to finalize the redlines before sending a DocuSign MOU.

—Ben
Partner Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

Eleanor — appreciate the fast turnaround. Summary of agreed pilot terms: 

1) Attribution: primary = first valid HubSpot registration (we will provide the registration URL and checklist).
2) Base split: 60/40 in favor of the registering partner for pilot deals.
3) Co-sell/demo: 30-day co-sell window; if both partners materially demo / contribute, default to 50/50 split for that opportunity unless a multi-party split form is signed at registration.
4) Clawback: 90 days for pilot contracts (prorated if partial refunds occur).
5) Billing: Redwood invoices hosting; ISV invoices license — term sheet must include end-to-end pricing and single-source discounting rules to avoid double discounts.

Next steps:
- Marissa will upload a redlined term sheet (attached) and a HubSpot registration checklist link: https://hubspot.company.com/deal/ACR-1337/register
- Ben will add the MSA addendum for data/security to the DocuSign packet.
- If Acera is aligned, we'll send an MOU via DocuSign: https://docusign.com/packet/ACR-1337-mou

Eleanor — can you confirm acceptance of the above and whether Acera needs any additional PO/contract language for the pilot? If yes, we'll route to legal (should be quick). If not, we'll send the DocuSign MOU by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot live.
